newsitem.title: MALTA: Malta unveils tax system to replace VAT.
newsitem.headline: Malta unveils tax system to replace VAT.

text.p: The Maltese government on Monday unveiled a new system of taxes to replace Value Added Tax, with 15 percent import duty on products from the European Union.
Non-EU imports will be subject to a levy of 35 percent more than imports from EU countries.
In a bill it intends moving in parliament later this month it also provided for a five percent excise tax on "any business sale in Malta made to a retailer" and a five percent tax on most services.
The taxes exclude essential goods and services such as food, medicines and educational and banking services.
They also do not apply to retailers with annual turnover below 12,000 Maltese pounds (about $31,200). Exporting companies are entitled tor refunds on tax paid on raw materials.
A lottery will be introduced to encourage customers to demand receipts.
The removal of VAT is credited as being one of the main factors in the Labour party's electoral victory in October.

Prime Minister Alfred Sant promised on Sunday that the new tax system would not increase the cost of living and in some areas prices could go down. The system, he said, would also cut administration costs for small businesses.

VAT was introduced in 1995 by the former Nationalist government at a uniform 15 percent, excluding essential services, as it prepared to take Malta into the European Union. The present government has frozen the EU application.
